newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: TIGER OATS SEES SLOWER SECOND HALF.
newsitem.headline: TIGER OATS SEES SLOWER SECOND HALF.

text.p: Food and pharmaceuticals group Tiger Oats Ltd said on Tuesday that it was unlikely to sustain first half growth levels, as there has been a slowdown in consumer spending in the past few months.
"Nonetheless, satisfactory real growth in headline earnings should be achieved for the year as a whole," the company said in a statement with first half results.
The company reported headline earnings per share up 21 percent to 210.9 cents for the six months to March 31, despite pressure on margins.
Tiger Foods saw earnings rise 15 percent while Langeberg and Adcock Ingram lifted earnings 10 and 15 percent respectively.
Managing director Nick Dennis said he was very satisfied with the results, although strong sales growth in Tiger Foods was offset somewhat by a squeeze on margins.
Langeberg performed well locally but headline earnings growth was held back to 10 percent by poor international results.
Dennis said last year's merger of Adcock Ingram and Premier Pharmceuticals was beginning to bear results and prospects were looking up for the second half.
With cash and cash equivalents at end-March exceeding borrowings by 870.7 million rand, the company said it was well placed to exploit future investment opportunities at home and abroad.
